To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
venture-backed IPOs are more underpriced compared to non venture-backed IPOs.
venture-backed IPOs are more underpriced, but have higher long-run abnormal returns than non venture-backed IPOs.

(1) the average underpricing of IPOs on the Neuer Markt is 18.4 percent, (2) venture capital-backed IPOs are more underpriced (on average by 4.7 percentage points) than non venture capital-backed IPOS, (3) bridge financings are not associated with lower underpricing and (4) IPOs underwritten by a prestigious bank show a significantly lower average underpricing (by 4.7 percent).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of venture capital in Germany's Neuer market.
the role of venture capitalists in the certification of the quality of a firm when going public.

the question of whether venture capitalists are able to provide additional certification to the IPO market and whether the certification effect of venture capitalists is more important than that of underwriters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the role of venture capitalists in certifying the IPO quality of a company is not as strong as expected, whereas the certification role of underwriters is more important.
the role of venture capital and the role of underwriters in IPOs are complementary.
the underpricing of IPOs on Germany's Neuer Mark is driven by the same factors as IPOs in other markets.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the role of venture capitalists as an additional certification mechanism is not yet established.
VC-backed and non VC-backed IPO companies differ with regard to their issuer and offering characteristics.
the role of venture capitalists in certifying the value of a company when it is going public is not as important as it is assumed by many.
The main takeaway from our work is that
venture-backed IPOs are more likely to be priced at a discount than IPOs without VC involvement.
VC-backed IPOs are underpriced because they are more likely to be overvalued.
the underwriter's certification is not as strong as expected.
